rules.title: Prohibition on sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or occupancy levels
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell or license to them, software that uses non-public competitor data (under 90 days old) to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels. A tenant whose landlord used such software can sue for injunctive relief, damages, civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, and attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (each month and each unit a separate violation)

coverage.summary: All residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. Excluded from the definition: aggregated, anonymous rental data reports that do not recommend rents; tools for setting affordable-housing rent or income limits; and market research for project financing, appraisals, or software research, testing, or training.

rules.exemptions: Excludes aggregated, anonymous rental data reports that do not recommend rents or terms; products used to set rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines; and information used for project-financing market research, appraisals, or software research, testing, or training (if competitor data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated). Competitor Data means non-public data under 90 days old about properties the landlord does not own or manage.
rules.penalty: The City Attorney may sue for damages, injunctive relief, restitution, and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation. An aggrieved tenant may sue for injunctive relief, money damages, and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation. The prevailing City Attorney or tenant is awarded attorney's fees and costs. Each month and each unit is a separate violation.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.interaction: Ordinance 7,992-N.S. amends the existing BMC Chapter 13.63, so the prohibition predates this amendment; the original start date is not stated. This ordinance was passed to print on November 18, 2025. Its final adoption date is not stated in the text; the URL suggests a December 2, 2025 second reading. If adopted then, it took effect about January 1, 2026 (30 days after adoption, Gov. Code § 36937). The text does not address state law (e.g., Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729).

notes: The document is the ordinance text as passed to print on November 18, 2025; it does not record the final adoption vote. Status in_force assumes adoption at the December 2, 2025 meeting indicated by the URL. effective_date is left null because Chapter 13.63 existed before this amendment and its original effective date is not given. The sale prohibition (§ 13.63.030(A)) and use prohibition (§ 13.63.030(B)) are combined in one record.
